name: Daniel Dennett
notes: Q4: rejects the experience vs brain-activity distinction. Q3/Q5: human consciousness is a culturally evolved user-illusion built by communication.

name: Todd Feinberg & Jon Ma
notes: Q7: affect and image-based consciousness arose together in the Cambrian. Q9: specific neural criteria met at a particular stage. Q6: they claim the gap is naturally explained.

name: Joseph LeDoux
notes: Q4: survival circuits do the work, feelings are cognitive constructions. Q10: insists on starting from human report.

name: Arthur Reber
notes: Q9: consciousness starts with the first cell, a definite point. Q6: says the hard problem dissolves once mind starts with life.

name: Axel Cleeremans
notes: Q3: consciousness is learned metarepresentation; unsure how widespread. Q5: social learning matters but not the main evolutionary purpose.

name: Kristin Andrews
notes: Q2: NY Declaration says realistic possibility for insects. Q10: argues against human-centred starting point.

name: Peter Halligan & David
notes: Q4: personal awareness is a passive by-product. Q5: its function is social broadcasting of internal content.
